summary: D0: explore Relational Wiki / Docs-as-Code / AI Context Engines for PRD-RFC-ADR alignment, synthesize an owned-substrate recommendation

research.category: Relational Wiki Solutions (graph/linked-doc wikis, relational-DB-as-wiki, ontology platforms, and the AST-fingerprint doc-binding tools that make them staleness-aware) — 2025-2026 state of the art

top_solutions.name: Backstage Software Catalog + TechDocs (CNCF / Spotify)
top_solutions.what: Open-source developer-portal catalog. Entities (Component/API/System/Domain/Resource/User/Group) are declared as YAML descriptors committed in-repo; a continuous processing loop parses each descriptor, emits typed directional relations (ownedBy/ownerOf, partOf/hasPart, dependsOn/dependencyOf, providesApi/consumesApi, parentOf/childOf, memberOf/hasMember), and 'stitches' them into one queryable software graph exposed via the catalog API. TechDocs renders per-entity markdown co-located with code and indexes it with the catalog in unified search. This is the closest production analog to oyatie's target: declared entities reconciled into a live relation graph.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: Relations are DERIVED from a single declared field (spec.owner, spec.dependsOn, spec.providesApis...), so the graph is generated, not co-authored on both ends — you cannot assert ownership two different ways. Reverse relations are auto-generated (ownedBy⇄ownerOf) so both directions are always in agreement by construction. Edges to a non-existent target surface as processing errors attached to the offending entity rather than silently disagreeing.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: The processor re-ingests descriptors continuously and records emit-edges between the producing and produced entities; orphan detection walks that graph so that when a root is unregistered, eager deletion cascades and any entity no longer reachable from a live source is flagged orphaned/stale. (Backstage issue #20030 — stale relations lingering after unregister — is evidence that the reconciler is the load-bearing AND the genuinely hard part.) Doc freshness itself relies on CI rebuilding TechDocs when source changes; it is structural (orphan/broken-ref), not semantic.
top_solutions.adoption_model: Self-hosted OSS (CNCF), plugin architecture, YAML-in-repo GitOps ingestion; commercial hardening via Spotify Portal, Roadie, and Port.
top_solutions.strengths: Proven declared-entity → reconciled-relation-graph model at org scale; in-repo GitOps source of truth; built-in orphan + broken-reference detection; custom entity/relation kinds are first-class (the 'well-known relations' are just a documented convention over a generic engine).
top_solutions.weaknesses: Relation vocabulary is dev-infra-centric with no native PRD/RFC/ADR kinds; staleness is structural (orphan/dangling), it does not know a doc semantically contradicts the code; heavy Node/TS runtime; catalog-drift is a real, paged, ongoing operational burden.

top_solutions.name: Palantir Foundry Ontology (object + link types)
top_solutions.what: Enterprise 'operational ontology' — object types (schemas of real-world entities) and link types (typed relationships, analogous to typed joins) backed by concrete datasources; a single semantic+kinetic+dynamic layer (objects, properties, links, actions, functions, security) that behaves as a live digital twin over the underlying data. The Ontology Metadata Service owns the type definitions; actions are the only sanctioned mutation path.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: One ontology = one canonical definition per object/link type. A link's existence is a FUNCTION of backing data (many-to-many links are materialized from their own datasource), not two hand-authored assertions, so the two ends cannot disagree. All writes flow through governed Actions, preventing divergent ad-hoc edits.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: Objects and links are materialized/derived from backing datasources, so the graph is a projection of the source-of-truth data rather than a maintained copy — when the data changes the ontology re-derives and cannot silently drift from what it is built on. (This is the key idea to steal: bind the graph to reality so freshness is automatic, not editorial.)
top_solutions.adoption_model: Proprietary, heavyweight enterprise platform — reference-only for methodology, never adopted directly.
top_solutions.strengths: Gold standard for 'typed links materialized from reality + single source of truth for both data AND logic'; the semantic/kinetic/dynamic layering is a clean model for structure vs. governed change vs. policy.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Closed and expensive; not a documentation tool per se; ties truth to datasets (oyatie's equivalent 'reality' endpoint is the code AST, not warehouse tables); no PRD/RFC/ADR notion out of the box.

top_solutions.name: Atlassian Rovo + Teamwork Graph (Confluence / Jira)
top_solutions.what: Confluence wiki + Jira issues sitting on a ~20-year 'Teamwork Graph' that maps typed relationships among pages, work items, people, and code. The Rovo GenAI assistant (GA 2025-2026, used by ~75% of the Fortune 500) answers by QUERYING the structured graph rather than running RAG over unstructured blobs.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: Explicit typed links between pages/issues/work items provide one navigable structure; related and conflicting items are surfaced via graph adjacency instead of being re-derived from text each time a question is asked.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: Weakest of the set for code-reality drift — the graph is maintained by humans plus AI edit suggestions, is page/issue-level rather than code-symbol-level, and has no AST binding to implementation. Freshness is essentially social/editorial.
top_solutions.adoption_model: Closed SaaS, bundled into paid Confluence/Jira Cloud tiers.
top_solutions.strengths: Large-scale real-world proof that graph-first beats RAG (their published 'graph over RAG' ARR-growth result); validates the core thesis that encoding structured relations once and querying the graph is the durable substrate.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Proprietary SaaS; docs↔code staleness effectively unsolved; the graph is org/work-centric, not architecture-decision-centric; not in-repo or GitOps.

top_solutions.name: Notion / Coda relational-databases-as-wiki
top_solutions.what: Document-first (Notion) and database-first (Coda) workspaces where pages live inside relational databases; relations + rollups + formulas connect databases, and (Notion's 2025 model) a database is a container over one or more data sources. Bidirectional relations plus backlinks form a lightweight wiki graph.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: The relation+rollup pattern is the takeaway: define a fact once in a source row, roll it up READ-ONLY everywhere else, so downstream views can never disagree with the source. Bidirectional relations keep both sides synchronized automatically (migrating to a tool without them requires re-creating lookups on both tables — evidence the auto-sync is doing real work).
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: Only within the workspace — rollups recompute from source rows, but there is zero binding to code or architecture reality: a Notion PRD has no idea the implementation changed. Staleness vs. reality is entirely manual.
top_solutions.adoption_model: Proprietary SaaS, no-code authoring, REST API for integration.
top_solutions.strengths: Best ergonomics anywhere for the 'relation + rollup = single source of truth, rendered into many views' pattern; extremely fast to model PRD/RFC/ADR as typed tables with relations.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Closed SaaS, not in-repo/GitOps, no code-reality anchor, weak at large-scale declarative constraint enforcement, export/lock-in risk.

top_solutions.name: Open file-native graph wikis: Obsidian (+Dataview) / Semantic MediaWiki / Wikibase
top_solutions.what: Markdown- and wiki-native knowledge graphs. Obsidian = local markdown, [[wikilinks]] producing automatic bidirectional backlinks + graph view + Dataview queries over YAML frontmatter, with vault-lint tools that flag broken links and orphans. Semantic MediaWiki / Wikibase = wiki pages carry typed statements (property:value triples) forming a real RDF/property knowledge graph with an ontology/schema and constraint validation — Wikibase is the engine behind Wikidata (~1.65B statements as of 2025).
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: Wikilinks are explicit typed references; SMW/Wikibase add typed statements plus property constraints so each page can be validated against the ontology (e.g., a decision must reference exactly one status, an entity must fill required properties). Dataview / constraint reports surface mismatches as queries.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: Structural and CI-runnable: broken-link, orphan, and frontmatter linters; SMW/Wikibase constraint reports flag statements violating the schema. No native AST/code binding, but frontmatter can carry a 'verified-against' anchor that a query checks — the hook where an AST-fingerprint check would plug in.
top_solutions.adoption_model: Obsidian = free local app + community plugins over portable markdown files (GitOps-friendly, fully ownable). SMW/Wikibase = OSS self-host on MediaWiki.
top_solutions.strengths: Fully open, file-native, portable, in-repo; bidirectional links + orphan/broken-link linting are exactly the primitives needed; Wikibase proves typed-statement graph + property constraints scale to billions of edges.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Obsidian's graph is untyped/link-only without plugins; SMW/Wikibase are PHP/MediaWiki-heavy; none bind to code AST natively; contradiction detection is only as strong as the constraint rules authored.

top_solutions.name: AST-fingerprint doc-to-code binding: fiberplane/drift & CI doc-drift detectors (the staleness engine)
top_solutions.what: Not a wiki — the code-reality staleness mechanism to reimplement. `drift` binds a doc anchor to a specific code target (file#Symbol) and stamps a NORMALIZED-AST fingerprint (tree-sitter parse → hash of node-kinds + token-text, stripping whitespace/position) into a drift.lock; `drift check` recomputes fingerprints and fails CI (exit 1) when the bound symbol's AST changed. Sibling Claude/GitHub-Actions doc-drift detectors compare docs against the merged diff on every PR.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: Indirect but useful — forces each doc claim to name exactly ONE code target, so ambiguity and duplicate ownership are caught at link time; a cross-repo `origin` field prevents false ownership across shared code.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: Best-in-class code-reality answer: content-addressed AST anchors mean any SEMANTIC change to the bound symbol flags the doc stale, while pure reformatting does not (near-zero false positives); `--changed` scopes checks to affected docs; it runs as a required merge gate — closing the gap that 'code goes through review + CI while docs go through nothing.'
top_solutions.adoption_model: OSS CLI, lockfile committed in-repo, CI-gated; language coverage via tree-sitter (TS/Python/Rust/Go/Zig/Java).
top_solutions.strengths: Precise, low-false-positive, symbol-level, CI-native; the missing binding between prose claims and the exact code that must stay true.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Anchors are hand-declared, so coverage requires discipline; it detects drift, not meaning (flags that code changed, not whether the doc is now wrong); it is not a graph — must be paired with a relation store to reason across PRD/RFC/ADR.

research.methodology_to_adopt: Reimplement, owned-Rust, the COMPOSITE that no single tool ships whole: a declared-typed-node/edge graph reconciled continuously (Backstage stitching + orphan detection), whose links are materialized from and anchored to reality (Foundry ontology-over-datasources; drift AST-fingerprint-over-code-symbols), guarded by declarative graph-constraint invariants (Semantic-MediaWiki/Wikibase property constraints; Foundry ontology validation). Concretely for PRD/RFC/ADR: (1) Model PRD-requirement, RFC/design-decision, ADR, and code-capability as typed nodes; every cross-document reference is a typed directional edge (PRD-requirement --realized_by--> RFC-decision --ratified_by--> ADR --implemented_by--> code-symbol), stored bidirectionally so backlinks and 'what depends on this' are free — exactly Backstage's derive-relations-from-one-declared-field trick so the two ends can never be authored into disagreement. (2) Every edge that targets code carries a normalized-AST fingerprint anchor (drift's mechanism: tree-sitter node-kinds+token-text hash, whitespace/position stripped); staleness = a fingerprint mismatch since the anchor was stamped, plus Backstage-style orphan/reachability detection for nodes no longer reachable from a live root. Freshness becomes a hash-compare on a required merge gate, not an editorial chore. (3) Contradiction = fail-closed graph-constraint queries in the exact shape of oyatie's EXISTING cross-artifact-agreement gate, just extended to the new node kinds: 'every RFC-decision resolves to exactly one Accepted ADR,' 'no two Accepted ADRs set the same capability property to different values,' 'a requirement cannot be Accepted in ADR-X and Superseded in ADR-Y without a supersession edge,' 'an ADR marked Accepted must propagate to masterplan∧roadmap∧spec' (already implemented) 'and to its parent PRD-requirement + child RFC.' (4) Run it LIVE like Backstage's processing loop / Foundry OMS — event-driven on commit, re-stitch the changed node's neighborhood, recompute fingerprints, re-evaluate the constraint pack — never a periodic batch export. Deliberately DO NOT adopt the SaaS graphs (Notion/Coda/Rovo/Foundry) as substrate; they are references behind an owned Rust port. ponytail note: the constraint evaluator is the same engine as the existing cross-artifact-agreement gate — extend node/edge kinds and rule set, do not build a second gate.
research.relevance_to_corpus_substrate: Maps 1:1 onto the founder-approved governance/corpus/ live AST/relational graph that replaces markdown-ADRs + JSON-SSOT. corpus already content-addresses the AST and tracks every fn/capability live — that IS the drift-style code-reality endpoint, so the AST-fingerprint staleness check is nearly free (compare the corpus node's content hash against the anchor stamped on the referencing edge; no separate tree-sitter pass needed because corpus is bespoke rowan-style per the W2 AST decision). Add PRD-requirement, RFC/design-decision, and ADR as first-class corpus NODE kinds alongside capability/decision (subsuming decisions.json + registry, which the corpus pivot already replaces), and the PRD→RFC→ADR→code chain becomes typed edges in the same graph rather than four disconnected markdown/JSON authorities — advancing the masterplan-v2 goal of reducing live md/json count and making every authority traceable. The Backstage stitching loop = the corpus reconciler; Foundry's 'graph is a projection of source-of-truth, not a maintained copy' = the corpus doctrine that decay is a fail-closed invariant and docs/directives are BUILD ARTIFACTS (rendered ADR/PRD/RFC markdown compiled OUT of the graph, never the source). The cross-artifact-agreement gate is already the constraint evaluator; this work is the natural extension the goal names — from ADR-spec-masterplan-roadmap agreement to PRD-RFC-ADR-capability agreement — using the same fail-closed 'Accepted must propagate' pattern already shipped.
research.portability_note: The engine ships three NEUTRAL primitives with zero PRD/RFC/ADR/oyatie semantics compiled in: (1) a typed content-addressed node/edge store, (2) a reconciler that recomputes anchor fingerprints + orphan reachability on change, (3) a constraint evaluator that runs declarative graph-query invariants. Everything domain-specific is policy-as-data loaded per repo: the ontology pack (node kinds, edge kinds, cardinalities), the anchor extractors (per-language AST-fingerprint plugins), and the invariant rule set. Backstage proves this shape — its 'well-known relations' are a documented CONVENTION over a generic entity+relation engine, and any adopter registers custom kinds; Foundry proves the ontology is data over a generic object/link backend; Wikibase proves typed-statement + property-constraint validation is schema-driven, not hardcoded. So oyatie sells the reconciler+evaluator as a product and any repo supplies its own ontology pack + rule pack + language anchor plugins — the same Cedar-style policy-as-data lens already in use for authz, applied to documentation governance. Acceptance question: could a Python or Go monorepo with no ADRs at all load a different ontology pack (say REQUIREMENT→TEST→MODULE) and get contradiction+staleness gating with zero engine changes? If not, oyatie-specific nuance has leaked into the engine and must be pushed back out into the pack.

research.category: Docs-as-Code Frameworks (versioned in-repo docs, CI-gated + linted, spec/ADR/RFC tooling) — 2025-2026 state of the art for PRD/RFC/ADR alignment, cross-document contradiction prevention, and staleness detection vs code/architecture reality

top_solutions.name: Structured MADR / MIF (Modeled Information Format) — machine-readable decisions-as-data
top_solutions.what: An extension of MADR (Markdown Any Decision Records) under the modeled-information-format org (smadr.dev, github.com/zircote/structured-madr). Every ADR is a Markdown file with a REQUIRED, JSON-Schema-validated YAML frontmatter block (title, description, type='adr', category, tags, status ∈ {proposed,accepted,deprecated,superseded}, created, updated, author, project, plus optional technologies/audience/related and a three-dimension risk assessment + categorized consequences + required audit section). Ships a JSON Schema + a GitHub Action validator (mif-validate) with tiered mifConformanceLevel 1/2/3. Complementary reference: joshrotenberg/adrs — an ADR tool in Rust that links ADRs and emits relationship graphs.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: Decisions become typed, schema-validated NODES rather than prose. The validator enforces referential integrity on relationship fields (supersedes/superseded_by/related) and status consistency across the set — a 'superseded' ADR must point at a live successor; an 'accepted' ADR whose successor supersedes it is a schema violation the CI Action rejects. Because metadata is machine-readable, 'two Accepted ADRs deciding the same subject oppositely' is detectable as a graph query, not left to human review.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: The four-state lifecycle (Proposed→Accepted→Deprecated/Superseded) plus immutability (never edit an Accepted ADR — write a superseding one) keeps the audit chain traversable; conformance-level CI blocks a merge that lands a status/link inconsistency. Weakness: on its own it detects staleness WITHIN the decision set (dangling links, orphaned status), not drift against live code — that requires binding ADR ids to code (the grep-for-'ADR-' test and CODEOWNERS-gated seams are the manual bridge).
top_solutions.adoption_model: Drop-in: adopt MADR templates, add the JSON Schema + GitHub Action to CI, pick a conformance level. Fully backward-compatible with plain-Markdown ADR workflows; incremental — start level 1, ratchet up.
top_solutions.strengths: Purest existing example of 'decisions as schema-validated data' — exactly the node contract a relational corpus needs. Neutral schema, policy-as-data conformance config, Rust tooling precedent (joshrotenberg/adrs) already emits decision graphs. Human-readable and machine-readable simultaneously.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Scope is ADRs only (no PRD/RFC node types, no requirement→design→decision traceability). Relationship vocabulary is thin (related/supersedes) — no first-class conflicts_with/refines/implements/derived_from edges. No code/architecture drift anchors. Validator is JS, not Rust.

top_solutions.name: GitHub Spec Kit — Spec-Driven Development (SDD) traceability chain
top_solutions.what: GitHub's open-source toolkit (github/spec-kit, 2025-2026) for Spec-Driven Development: an artifact chain Constitution → Specify → Plan → Tasks → Implement, each a Markdown artifact feeding the next. Inverts the model so the spec/PRD is the SOURCE that generates implementation, not a guide for it. Ships slash-commands/skills for 29+ AI agents (incl. Claude Code, Codex).
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: This is the strongest current answer to PRD/RFC/ADR alignment specifically. (1) Bidirectional linking: every technology choice in the Plan traces to a specific requirement in the Spec; every API contract links to a user story; every test scenario to an acceptance criterion. (2) Continuous consistency validation explicitly flags 'spec requires X but plan assumes Y' BEFORE code generation — cross-level contradiction detection between the PRD-tier (spec) and RFC-tier (plan). (3) Templates act as 'unit tests for specifications' — completeness checks + constitutional-compliance phase gates (Simplicity/Anti-Abstraction/Integration-First) that require documented justification to bypass.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: Living documentation via GENERATION: when requirements change you edit the spec FIRST, and the change cascades — affected plan decisions flag, code regenerates — eliminating spec/code divergence at the source. Mandatory [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers force declaration of unknowns (an ambiguity gate, structurally identical to Ouroboros/oyatie's ambiguity≤0.2 doctrine) so ambiguous language cannot proceed downstream. Production feedback (incidents/metrics) is an explicit input to the next spec iteration.
top_solutions.adoption_model: Per-repo toolkit installed alongside an AI coding agent; presets restructure templates for regulatory traceability, methodology (Agile/DDD/etc.), or added security/test-first gates. Methodology-first — value is the artifact chain + gates, portable independent of the CLI.
top_solutions.strengths: Directly models the PRD→RFC→(ADR-embedded-in-plan)→tasks→code chain with forced traceability and cross-level contradiction flags; the phase-gate + forced-uncertainty-marker pattern is exactly reusable as owned graph invariants. Current, GitHub-backed, AI-native.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Contradiction/consistency checks are LLM-driven (probabilistic, not a deterministic graph invariant) — evidence-admissibility risk. Artifacts are per-feature Markdown, not a persistent cross-feature relational graph, so it doesn't detect contradictions between two OLD specs. No formal decision-node model (ADRs live inside plan prose).

top_solutions.name: Backstage Software Catalog + TechDocs — the reference relational knowledge graph for docs
top_solutions.what: Spotify's Backstage (CNCF) pairs a Software Catalog (entities — System/Component/API/Resource/User/Group — declared in catalog-info.yaml with TYPED relations: ownedBy, dependsOn, providesApi, partOf) with TechDocs, a docs-like-code plugin that builds Markdown via MkDocs and binds each doc site to its catalog entity. 'The documentation isn't just text; it's connected knowledge.'
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: The catalog IS a relational graph — docs are attached to entities that have machine-checkable relationships, so a doc claiming a dependency the catalog graph doesn't have is a queryable inconsistency. Custom plugins pull external docs into one unified, entity-linked search surface, reducing the 'two documents describe the same system differently' failure by giving every doc a single canonical entity anchor.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: Docs live in the same repo as code and are tied to the catalog entity, so ownership/relations drift is visible against the graph; catalog processors continuously re-ingest catalog-info.yaml so entity relationships track reality. Weakness: TechDocs staleness detection for the PROSE body is weak — it renders whatever Markdown exists; freshness is mostly 'co-located so more likely updated,' not enforced.
top_solutions.adoption_model: Platform adoption (developer portal), heavier than a linter — run Backstage, register entities, co-locate docs. Enterprise-grade; the relational-graph model is the reusable idea even if you don't run Backstage.
top_solutions.strengths: The canonical existing 'docs-as-code + structured relational knowledge graph' — exactly the shape oyatie is moving toward (loose cloud folders → relational graph). Typed-entity + typed-relation model is a proven edge vocabulary to mirror. Docs bound to entities, not floating.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Node/edge model is service-catalog-shaped, not decision/requirement-shaped (no ADR/RFC/PRD node types or supersedes/conflicts edges out of the box). Heavy TypeScript platform, not Rust. Contradiction detection is not built-in — you'd add it.

top_solutions.name: Structurizr DSL / C4 model-as-code + architecture fitness functions (ArchUnit/Deptrac)
top_solutions.what: Structurizr (docs.structurizr.com) is 'models as code' for the C4 model: you author ONE plaintext DSL model of the architecture (Context/Container/Component/Code) in version control and render many diagrams from it — a single queryable source of truth for system structure. Paired with fitness-function linters — ArchUnit (Java), Deptrac (PHP), go-arch-lint (Go) — that couple structural constraints to CI so architecture violations fail the build.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: Makes 'architectural reality' itself a machine-readable model, so an RFC/ADR that describes a boundary the model doesn't contain is a checkable divergence. One model → all diagrams eliminates the classic contradiction of several hand-drawn diagrams disagreeing.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: This is the strongest staleness pattern in the set. Architecture fitness functions run in CI and — critically — can be configured to block ONLY net-new violations, so drift can decrease but never silently increase (a ratchet). Structurizr's plaintext model diffs in Git; ArchSteer-style tools track a drift index over time. Binding docs to the model/code (path globs, C4 element ids) turns staleness from a quarterly manual audit into a per-merge mechanical gate.
top_solutions.adoption_model: DSL file(s) in-repo + a renderer; fitness-function libs wired into CI. Incremental — add one constraint at a time. Model-as-code portable to any repo.
top_solutions.strengths: Supplies the 'architecture reality as a queryable node' that PRD/RFC/ADR claims can be validated AGAINST, plus the net-new-only ratchet that matches oyatie's merge-base ratchet doctrine exactly. Deterministic, not LLM-based.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Describes structure, not requirements or decisions — complements, doesn't replace, the decision graph. Fitness-function tools are language-specific (Java/PHP/Go); an owned-Rust equivalent must be built. Model can itself go stale if not regenerated from code.

top_solutions.name: Spectral (+ Vale) — the neutral-engine + policy-as-data linting archetype
top_solutions.what: Spectral (Stoplight, open source) is a generic JSON/YAML linter where an engine evaluates RULESETS-AS-DATA (each rule = a `given` JSONPath selector + a `then` function/assertion), with built-in support for OpenAPI 3.x, AsyncAPI, Arazzo, JSON Schema. Vale (vale.sh) is the prose analogue: a markup-aware engine that evaluates style/terminology packages-as-data (Microsoft/Google styles, custom vocabularies) across Markdown/AsciiDoc/rST. Both run in Git hooks/CI; both are 2025-2026 current and widely adopted (Adidas, Azure, Box, Elastic, Grafana ship rulesets).
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: Vale enforces one canonical vocabulary/terminology across every document, killing the low-level contradiction class where PRD/RFC/ADR use divergent terms for the same concept. Spectral enforces structural/naming/consistency invariants over any structured artifact — the exact mechanism you'd point at frontmatter to assert 'status field consistency' or 'required cross-reference present.'
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: Indirect — they catch style/terminology/structural drift on every merge, not code-vs-doc semantic staleness. Their real contribution here is architectural: proof that a NEUTRAL engine + POLICY-AS-DATA rulesets is the right factoring for a portable governance product.
top_solutions.adoption_model: Single binary + a ruleset/style file per repo; extend or author org rulesets. The purest 'engine ships once, policy ships as data per repo' model.
top_solutions.strengths: The template for the portability requirement: engine is domain-agnostic, all the opinion lives in loadable data. Enormous prior art in published rulesets. Trivial CI integration.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Text/structure-level only — no cross-artifact relational graph, no requirement traceability, no code-drift semantics. Node.js engines. You reuse the ARCHITECTURE, not the tools.

top_solutions.name: CI doc-drift detection (code→doc mapping tables + semantic diff on merge)
top_solutions.what: The emerging 2025-2026 pattern (e.g., the doc-drift GitHub Action using an explicit CLAUDE.md mapping table, plus the general 'docs as build artifacts' discipline): on PR merge, extract the code diff and check it against the docs an explicit mapping table says it affects ('src/api/ → docs/api/', 'src/auth/ → docs/guides/authentication.md'), then open a follow-up doc-fix PR when drift is found.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: Weak on cross-DOCUMENT contradiction (it's code↔doc, not doc↔doc) — but the mapping-table idea generalizes: a declared, machine-readable map from a code region/capability to the docs that describe it is the anchor the corpus needs to make every drift check deterministic instead of guesswork.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: This is the core staleness mechanism in the set: a maintained mapping table (or richer: fingerprints/anchors) means every merge mechanically asks 'does any changed code region have a doc that now describes stale behavior?' Treating docs as build artifacts subject to the same CI discipline as binaries (build + lint + link-check block merge like a failing test) is the enforcement doctrine.
top_solutions.adoption_model: GitHub Action + a mapping file in-repo. Cheap to adopt; today's implementations are LLM-diff-based (per-run cost, no memory between runs).
top_solutions.strengths: Concretely operationalizes 'staleness = process failure needing a mechanical detector' — the mapping table is the missing edge type (doc-node → code-anchor) the corpus graph must add. Auto-remediation (opens the fix PR) matches automation-maximalism.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Current implementations are LLM-semantic (probabilistic, evidence-admissibility risk, no deterministic checksum/fingerprint anchoring) and stateless. The mapping table is hand-maintained and itself goes stale. Needs to be re-grounded as deterministic graph anchors, not a per-run LLM judgment.

research.methodology_to_adopt: Reimplement, owned-Rust, the union of five deterministic mechanisms — NOT any single tool — as one graph+invariant engine: (1) DOCS-AS-TYPED-NODES WITH A SCHEMA-VALIDATED EDGE MODEL (from MIF/Structured MADR + Backstage relations): every PRD/RFC/ADR ingested into governance/corpus/ as a node with a machine-readable, serde-validated contract (id, status, tier=PRD|RFC|ADR) and FIRST-CLASS typed edges — supersedes/superseded_by, refines, implements, derived_from, and conflicts_with — with referential-integrity + status-consistency + orphan-link checks as GRAPH INVARIANTS, not prose review. This is the missing richness over MADR's thin `related`. (2) BIDIRECTIONAL REQUIREMENT→DESIGN→DECISION→CODE TRACEABILITY WITH FORCED-UNCERTAINTY GATES (from Spec Kit): every RFC clause must cite the PRD requirement it satisfies and every ADR the RFC section it realizes; unresolved gaps are explicit NEEDS_CLARIFICATION nodes that BLOCK promotion (your existing ambiguity≤0.2 / Ouroboros doctrine, made structural). (3) CROSS-DOCUMENT CONTRADICTION AS DETERMINISTIC GRAPH QUERIES over that relational graph — a `conflicts_with` edge, or two Accepted nodes deciding the same subject oppositely, or an RFC contradicting an Accepted ADR, is a failing invariant. This is literally your existing cross-artifact-agreement gate + the `unpropagated_decision`/'ADR-Accepted-must-propagate' rule, generalized from ADR-spec-masterplan-roadmap to add PRD and RFC node/edge types. (4) STALENESS AS FITNESS FUNCTIONS BINDING DOCS TO REALITY (from ArchUnit/Structurizr/doc-drift mapping tables): each doc node carries DETERMINISTIC anchors — path globs, AST symbol ids, C4/architecture-model element ids, capability ids — and a reconciler computes drift every merge, failing CI on NET-NEW drift only (the ratchet, matching your merge-base doctrine). Replace the LLM-semantic doc-drift check with these deterministic anchors so evidence is admissible. (5) POLICY-AS-DATA RULE EVALUATION (from Spectral/Vale): contradiction, staleness, and terminology rules are DATA (an owned Policy IR — your currently-OPEN question — evaluated as graph invariants; Vale-style vocabularies for terminology), not hardcoded Rust. Transient references (Spectral rule-shape, MIF JSON Schema as the node contract, Backstage typed-relations as the edge vocabulary, Structurizr as the architecture-reality node) sit behind owned ports; the destination is the live AST/relational graph evaluated by an owned deterministic invariant runtime.
research.portability_note: The product must factor exactly like Spectral (linter core + ruleset-as-data) and Vale (engine + style packages) and MIF (validator + conformance-level config): a NEUTRAL Rust engine — a graph store + a deterministic invariant evaluator + a drift reconciler — with ZERO oyatie nuance compiled in. Every domain-specific thing is policy-as-data loaded per repo: the node schemas (what a PRD/RFC/ADR is), the edge vocabulary (supersedes/refines/implements/conflicts_with), the drift-anchor resolvers (which code/architecture facts a doc binds to), the promotion/ambiguity thresholds, and the contradiction rulepacks. No hardcoded ADR-numbering (ADR-0xxx), no baked-in capability names, no oyatie tier names — a fresh repo supplies its own schemas + edge dialect + rulepacks and gets the same guarantees. Follow the MIF conformance-level model (levels 1/2/3) so any repo can adopt incrementally and ratchet up. The shippable unit is 'graph engine + invariant runtime + reconciler'; the corpus content and rulepacks are the data plane. This mirrors the memory doctrine: adopt best-in-class methodology, reimplement owned-Rust behind an owned port, keep the engine universal + productized + hermetic so the ratchet runs on ANY repo, not just oyatie.
research.relevance_to_corpus_substrate: Direct and load-bearing: everything the founder-approved governance/corpus/ live AST/relational graph wants (every capability/decision tracked live, docs+directives as BUILD ARTIFACTS rendered FROM the graph, markdown-ADRs + JSON-SSOT retired) is precisely the union of these solutions' proven mechanisms — Backstage supplies the relational entity+typed-edge model, MIF/Structured MADR supplies the schema-validated decision-node contract, Spec Kit supplies the PRD→RFC→ADR→code traceability chain + forced-clarification gate, Structurizr supplies architecture-as-a-queryable-node, and Spectral/ArchUnit supply the policy-as-data invariant + net-new-only drift ratchet. Crucially, oyatie has ALREADY BUILT THE SEED of exactly this engine: the cross-artifact-agreement gate that enforces ADR-spec-masterplan-roadmap agreement, plus the 'ADR-Accepted-must-propagate' / `unpropagated_decision` invariant. The D0 docs-maintenance exploration (task #5, workflow wlxyve2vr) should therefore frame the PRD-RFC-ADR extension NOT as a new subsystem but as (a) two new node types (PRD, RFC) + new edge types (satisfies, realizes, conflicts_with, derived_from) in that existing graph, (b) NEEDS_CLARIFICATION nodes as a promotion-blocking ambiguity gate, and (c) deterministic code/architecture drift anchors replacing prose review — all evaluated by the same owned invariant runtime that already exists. Under the corpus model, the markdown ADRs, the RFC/PRD docs, the ADR index, and the JSON SSOT all become PROJECTIONS (build artifacts) generated from the graph, so contradiction becomes structurally impossible (one source, many rendered faces) and staleness becomes a mechanical per-merge fitness-function fail rather than a quarterly manual audit.

research.category: AI-Driven Context Engines (LLM-indexed knowledge graphs + hybrid retrieval + semantic contradiction/staleness detection over PRD/RFC/ADR + code corpora)

top_solutions.name: Microsoft GraphRAG (LLM-extracted typed graph + claim/covariate extraction + Leiden community detection)
top_solutions.what: Open-source (20k+ stars, July 2024) framework that autonomously builds a knowledge graph from unstructured text: LLMs extract entities (nodes), relationships (edges), and — critically — 'covariates', i.e. typed CLAIMS carrying an evaluated status (TRUE/FALSE/SUSPECTED), time-bounds, and source provenance. Hierarchical Leiden community detection clusters related nodes; communities are auto-summarized into hierarchical reports for graph-aware retrieval. Claim extraction is a separable workflow (off by default) — that separability is exactly what makes it portable as a doc-governance primitive.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: The covariate/claim layer is the mechanism: each PRD requirement, RFC design decision, and ADR ruling is extracted as a typed claim node attached to a shared subject entity. Contradictions surface as conflicting claim-status on the same entity across documents, with source-provenance tracking that names WHICH doc conflicts. A regulatory-domain study (DORA-EU vs FFIEC-US) showed the graph structure collapses contradiction-detection cost from O(n^2) pairwise-chunk comparison to O(k·n) (k = neighbors sharing a subject) with a ~734x token reduction versus brute-force LLM pairing — the key efficiency argument for doing it on a graph rather than over flat text.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: Time-bounds + status on each claim let the graph carry temporal validity; community re-summarization on re-index re-derives the current state. Weak on code-reality drift by itself — it indexes text, not the running code/AST — so it needs an external code-anchor (see Cursor/Swimm) to close the code-vs-doc loop.
top_solutions.adoption_model: Apache-2.0 Python library + Azure reference; self-host or managed. Reference-only for oyatie (Python, LLM-per-extraction cost).
top_solutions.strengths: Typed-claim-with-status is the single most reusable primitive for cross-doc contradiction; graph structure gives provable O(k·n) contradiction cost; hierarchical community summaries scale to large corpora.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Expensive LLM indexing; Python; batch/re-index model (not incremental-first); no native code-reality anchor; claim extraction quality is prompt-sensitive.

top_solutions.name: NLI-backed Contradiction-Mining pipeline (LegalWiz multi-agent; arXiv 2508.17127 targeted entailment/contradiction)
top_solutions.what: A modular retrieve -> classify -> judge pipeline that is the current SOTA methodology for cross-document contradiction. LegalWiz's Contradiction Mining Agent = semantic-similarity retriever + a Natural Language Inference (NLI) classifier (entailment/neutral/CONTRADICTION) + an LLM-judge, detecting both intra-document (self) and inter-document (pairwise) conflicts. arXiv 2508.17127 refines candidate selection: aggregate transformer attention scores to retrieve contextually-relevant candidate sentences, run NLI on each pair, then saliency-filter to keep only significant relations.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: This IS the contradiction detector. A retriever prunes the O(n^2) claim-pair space to a small candidate set (embedding similarity or attention), an NLI model labels each surviving PRD/RFC/ADR statement pair, and an LLM-judge triages false positives. Directly answers 'does this ADR ruling contradict that PRD requirement?' as a classification over retrieved pairs rather than whole-corpus scan.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: Not its job — it detects logical conflict between two texts, not drift vs code. Pair it with a code-anchored freshness layer. Its value is the triage architecture (retriever -> NLI -> judge -> human review) that keeps precision high and audits clear.
top_solutions.adoption_model: Research pipelines; NLI = a fine-tuned encoder (DeBERTa/RoBERTa-MNLI class) usable as an owned Rust inference adapter behind a port; LLM-judge = subscription-pooled model. Methodology, not a product.
top_solutions.strengths: Precise, auditable, modular; retriever stage makes it tractable at corpus scale; NLI is a small, ownable model (no giant LLM required for the classify step).
top_solutions.weaknesses: Two-model cost (NLI + judge); NLI trained on generic MNLI misses domain/antonym nuance (contradiction-specific embeddings help); needs the retriever tuned or recall drops.

top_solutions.name: Cursor / Sourcegraph Cody / Augment Context Engine (Merkle-incremental code graph + embeddings)
top_solutions.what: Production code-context engines. Cursor chunks code locally, builds a Merkle tree of cryptographic content hashes, syncs only divergent chunks to a vector DB (Turbopuffer), re-checks every ~5 min. Cody uses Sourcegraph's Code Graph (symbol/relationship graph + remote-repo awareness) for architecturally-consistent retrieval. Augment builds a 400k-file semantic dependency graph with persistent 'Memories' and millisecond sync, explicitly claiming to 'detect architectural drift and breaking changes before they merge'.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: Indirect — the code graph gives relationship-aware retrieval (what connects to what), so a doc claim can be checked against the actual dependency/symbol graph rather than isolated text. Not a doc-vs-doc contradiction engine.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: This is the best-in-class STALENESS methodology. The Merkle tree of content hashes is an incremental change detector: compare candidate-tree hashes to indexed-tree hashes, re-embed only where they diverge, skip matches. This is exactly the freshness primitive oyatie already has (scm-facts/materializer content hashing). Augment/Cody extend it to a live dependency graph that flags drift/breakage pre-merge.
top_solutions.adoption_model: Commercial SaaS (Cursor/Augment) + source-available (Cody snapshot). Reference-only; the Merkle-freshness + code-graph-retrieval design is the transferable part.
top_solutions.strengths: Merkle/content-hash freshness is cheap, incremental, deterministic, and repo-agnostic; code-graph retrieval is relationship-aware not just semantic; proven at 400k-file scale.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Closed engines; embeddings live in remote vector DBs; freshness detects that a hash changed, not whether the change invalidates a specific doc claim (needs the claim<->anchor link layer on top).

top_solutions.name: Swimm living-docs / code-coupled documentation + Doc-Drift CI gate
top_solutions.what: Swimm authors docs with 'Smart Tokens' and code snippets anchored to specific source symbols; a patented Auto-sync algorithm re-verifies each anchor on code change and flags the doc stale when the change is impactful. A CI gate fails the PR when referenced code changed but the doc did not. The lightweight open pattern (doc-drift-in-CI) uses a code-to-docs mapping table + on-merge trigger + LLM diff-vs-docs surface-reference check, opening a follow-up PR.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: Not cross-doc — it's doc-vs-code coupling. Prevents the doc from silently disagreeing with the code it documents.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: Best-in-class doc-vs-code-REALITY staleness at product level: bind each doc claim to a concrete code anchor (symbol/span), and when the anchor's content changes, the binding breaks -> doc auto-flagged stale -> merge blocked until reconciled. The CI-gate-on-every-merge cadence (not quarterly audit) is the key operational pattern; staleness is treated as a mechanical, blocking signal.
top_solutions.adoption_model: Swimm = commercial SaaS + IDE/CI plugins; doc-drift-CI = an open GitHub-Actions + LLM recipe. Adopt the METHODOLOGY (anchor binding + on-merge blocking gate), not the tool.
top_solutions.strengths: Turns staleness into a deterministic, blocking CI signal tied to real code anchors; author-gated to prevent prompt-injection; low cost when anchors are symbol-level.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Surface-reference matching misses IMPLIED/semantic drift (rename userCache->sessionStore reads as trivial); needs an explicit code-to-docs mapping kept in sync; no cross-document reasoning.

top_solutions.name: SHACL/OWL graph validation + Architecture Reflexion Model (policy-as-data constraint + code-vs-design drift)
top_solutions.what: SHACL (W3C) validates a knowledge graph against declarative 'shapes' under a CLOSED-world assumption — it rejects updates that violate constraints; OWL reasoning adds OPEN-world inference to derive implicit facts. The Reflexion Model (architecture conformance) compares a source model abstracted from code against a high-level model of the design/ADR decisions and reports the gaps as architectural drift.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: SHACL shapes encode invariants like 'every PRD requirement MUST trace to >=1 RFC design node and its ADR ruling MUST NOT contradict the requirement's status' — a violating edit is rejected at write time. This is the declarative gate that turns oyatie's existing cross-artifact-agreement rule into portable data instead of code.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: The Reflexion Model is the code-vs-ARCHITECTURE drift methodology: extract the real dependency/module graph from code, overlay the ADR-declared intended architecture, and the delta IS the drift. Convergence (matched), divergence (code has edge design forbids), absence (design edge code lacks) are the three drift verdicts.
top_solutions.adoption_model: SHACL/OWL = open W3C standards with mature validators; Reflexion = academic + some tooling. Both are methodologies/standards, not products — ideal to reimplement owned-Rust.
top_solutions.strengths: Policy-as-data: constraints are declarative shapes loaded at runtime, zero domain nuance in the engine — exactly the neutral-engine requirement; closed-world SHACL gives fail-closed write rejection; Reflexion gives a rigorous code<->design drift verdict.
top_solutions.weaknesses: RDF/OWL toolchains are heavy and academic; SHACL alone can't detect NL contradiction (needs the NLI layer); Reflexion needs an accurate code-model extractor (the AST graph oyatie already builds).

top_solutions.name: Spec-Driven Development substrates (GitHub Spec-Kit, OpenSpec, AWS Kiro, Tessl) — spec-as-source-of-truth lifecycle
top_solutions.what: The 2025-2026 practice where versioned, STRUCTURED specifications (not code) are the source of truth and code is generated/checked against them. The spec-driven-with-ADR schema keeps ADRs living alongside the SSOT spec, outside any single change, so context persists across changes. Traditional design docs are advisory; SDD specs are ENFORCED — tests fail when code diverges.
top_solutions.contradiction_prevention: Structural: PRD-level intent, RFC-level behavior contract (I/O, pre/postconditions, invariants, interface types, state machines), and ADR decisions are distinct-but-linked artifacts in ONE versioned graph, so a change updates the shared spec rather than forking a contradicting copy. The change-proposal lifecycle (OpenSpec) forces edits through the spec, preventing divergent side-docs.
top_solutions.staleness_prevention: Enforcement, not advice: specs are executable contracts and tests fail if code diverges (spec-as-source regenerates code rather than hand-editing). Staleness becomes a failing check, not a manual audit.
top_solutions.adoption_model: Spec-Kit/OpenSpec = OSS conventions + CLIs; Kiro/Tessl = products. Adopt the lifecycle model (versioned structured spec graph, ADRs alongside, change-proposals, enforced-not-advisory), reimplement as commit-only writes to the corpus graph.
top_solutions.strengths: Closest conceptual match to oyatie's north star (structured spec graph as SSOT, docs as enforced artifacts); the PRD/RFC/ADR separation-with-links is already the target taxonomy; enforced-contract framing kills advisory-doc rot.
top_solutions.weaknesses: Most implementations are markdown-file conventions (the very thing oyatie is replacing) + LLM regeneration; contradiction detection is structural only unless an NLI/graph layer is added; ecosystem is fragmented across 8+ incompatible flavors.

research.methodology_to_adopt:
Reimplement, owned-Rust, a composite of four proven primitives — this is the specific methodology, deliberately unbundled from any single tool:

1. TYPED-CLAIM (covariate) EXTRACTION over the graph (from GraphRAG): every PRD requirement, RFC design decision, and ADR ruling is extracted/registered as a typed claim NODE carrying {subject entity, status, time-bounds, source provenance = content-hash of the exact source span}. Extraction runs through an owned Rust port with an embedding+LLM adapter (subscription-pooled models behind the port; NLI = a small ownable encoder). This is what makes cross-doc contradiction a graph query instead of an O(n^2) text scan (proven O(k·n), ~734x fewer tokens).

2. RETRIEVE -> NLI -> LLM-JUDGE contradiction triage (from LegalWiz / arXiv 2508.17127): for any two claims sharing a subject, a Rust retriever (embedding/attention similarity) prunes candidate pairs, a Rust-hosted NLI model classifies entailment/neutral/CONTRADICTION, and an LLM-judge triages. This is the actual PRD<->RFC<->ADR contradiction detector and extends the existing cross-artifact-agreement gate to a semantic (not just structural) predicate.

3. MERKLE / CONTENT-HASH FRESHNESS ANCHORING (from Cursor/Augment + oyatie's own scm-facts/materializer): bind each claim to a code/AST anchor by content hash; incrementally diff candidate-tree hashes vs indexed-tree hashes; a hash change on an anchor auto-flags the bound claim STALE. This is the doc-vs-code-reality detector, done incrementally and deterministically. Overlay the Reflexion-Model verdict (convergence/divergence/absence) to get code-vs-ARCHITECTURE drift against ADR-declared intent.

4. SHACL-STYLE DECLARATIVE CONSTRAINT SHAPES as the fail-closed gate (from SHACL/OWL): all agreement/traceability/invariant rules ('every PRD req traces to an RFC design + non-contradicting ADR ruling', 'an Accepted ADR must propagate') are declarative shapes evaluated closed-world at write time; a violating commit is rejected. This is the blocking, mechanical enforcement layer (matches oyatie's automation-maximalism + fail-closed doctrine).

The operating cadence is Swimm's: run the gate on EVERY merge (continuous, blocking), not on a periodic audit — staleness and contradiction are treated as mechanical CI signals, not review opinions.
research.relevance_to_corpus_substrate:
governance/corpus/ is already the founder-approved live AST/relational graph replacing markdown-ADRs + JSON-SSOT, with the Corpus Liveness Graph doctrine (content-addressed AST graph, decay = fail-closed invariants, docs/directives = build artifacts) and an existing cross-artifact-agreement gate (ADR-spec-masterplan-roadmap). The methodology drops straight in:

- NEW NODE TYPES: add PRDRequirement, RFCDesignDecision, ADRRuling as first-class typed claim nodes in the corpus graph (they are GraphRAG covariates with status + time-bounds + provenance). No new SSOT files — they are graph entities, extending the existing decisions/registry the corpus already subsumes.
- NEW EDGE TYPES: traceability edges PRDRequirement --realized_by--> RFCDesignDecision --ratified_by--> ADRRuling --implements--> CapabilityNode(code AST). The corpus already tracks every fn/capability live, so the ADR->code edge reuses existing anchors.
- CONTRADICTION as a graph query + NLI: run the retrieve->NLI->judge pass over sibling claims sharing a subject entity; a CONTRADICTION verdict is a fail-closed invariant violation (same shape as the existing 'unpropagated_decision: Accepted must reach masterplan/roadmap/spec' rule), extending cross-artifact-agreement from 4 artifacts to the PRD-RFC-ADR triple.
- STALENESS reuses what exists: the corpus is content-addressed and oyatie's scm-facts/materializer already computes content hashes; bind each claim's provenance to that hash and a mismatch = STALE (decay = fail-closed). The Reflexion overlay compares the live code AST subgraph to the ADR-declared intended architecture for drift.
- The whole thing is authored as an IMPLEMENTATION of the existing ADR cluster (corpus pivot + cross-artifact-agreement gate), not a fresh design — new claim/edge types + NLI-contradiction and freshness shapes added to the corpus, docs regenerated as build artifacts.
research.portability_note:
Neutral engine + policy-as-data throughout — no oyatie nuance compiled in:

ENGINE (universal, ships to any repo): the Rust graph store, the claim-extraction port (embedding/NLI/LLM adapters swappable behind the trait), the Merkle/content-hash freshness differ, the retrieve->NLI->judge contradiction runner, and the SHACL-style constraint evaluator. None of these know what a 'PRD' or an 'ADR' is — they operate on typed nodes, typed edges, content-hash anchors, and declarative shapes.

POLICY-AS-DATA (per-repo, loaded at runtime): the node/edge TAXONOMY (which artifact types exist: PRD/RFC/ADR here, could be Epic/Story/Spec elsewhere), the traceability RULES (which edges are mandatory), the INVARIANT shapes (what counts as a contradiction, what must propagate), and the code-to-anchor MAPPING all live as declarative rulepacks/shapes — data the engine loads, never branches it embeds. This mirrors the founder-refined policy-pack substrate direction (one pack lifecycle, split evaluation, Cedar/SHACL as benchmark-dialect not north star) and the reorg neutral-destination doctrine.

Adapters absorb transient infra (any embedding model, any NLI encoder, any vector index) behind owned ports whose trait shapes model the W5 destination, so the cutover from transient models to owned inference changes an adapter, not the engine. Result: a portable product — drop the engine into any repo, hand it that repo's taxonomy + constraint pack + anchor mapping as data, and it enforces PRD/RFC/ADR (or any doc-triad) agreement and freshness with zero code change. Passes the 'would AWS/Google ship this as a neutral product?' bar because the differentiated logic is entirely in the swappable policy pack.

synthesis.recommendation:
Adopt all three research categories, but as three COMPLEMENTARY LAYERS collapsed into ONE evaluator extension — not three subsystems. Ranked by load-bearing weight: (1) Docs-as-Code discipline is the SPINE — every PRD/RFC/ADR becomes a serde-validated typed node with a machine-readable frontmatter contract + forced traceability (MIF/Structured-MADR node contract + GitHub Spec-Kit PRD→RFC→ADR→code chain with NEEDS_CLARIFICATION promotion gate). (2) The Relational Wiki / graph model is the SUBSTRATE — governance/corpus/ stores those nodes as a live typed node/edge graph where reverse edges are DERIVED from one declared end (Backstage's derive-relations-from-one-declared-field trick, so the two ends can never be authored into disagreement) and the graph is a PROJECTION of reality, not a maintained copy (Foundry ontology-over-datasources; oyatie's equivalent 'reality' endpoint is the code AST the corpus already content-addresses). Rendered markdown ADR/PRD/RFC become BUILD ARTIFACTS compiled OUT of the graph, so contradiction is structurally impossible (one source, many faces). (3) The AI Context Engine is adopted ADVISORY-ONLY, never as an enforcing gate — GraphRAG typed-claims framing informs the node model, and a retrieve→NLI→judge semantic-contradiction pass runs as a non-blocking second opinion that FILES AN ISSUE, never a merge verdict, because LLM/NLI verdicts fail oyatie's evidence-admissibility bar (the LLM-benchmark-evidence-admissibility lesson: a lane that self-grades toward PASS is the danger). Deterministic graph invariants + content-hash drift anchors are the ONLY blocking layer.

CRITICAL grounding: do NOT build a new subsystem. The cross-artifact-agreement gate (cloud/cloud-ci/gates/oya-cloud-ci-cross-artifact-agreement-app/src/lib.rs) is ALREADY this engine — a pure fixture-driven evaluator over a corpus Value emitting keyed {code,key} findings with a net-new ratchet and carve-outs-as-DATA. The staleness-reaper gate already ships TTL+reachability with report-not-reap. The ADR frontmatter already carries reciprocal supersedes/superseded_by, depends_on, related_specs, and affected_surfaces.crates (the ADR→code edge); DD-NNNN design docs are oyatie's RFC tier. The whole PRD-RFC-ADR extension is therefore (a) two new node kinds (PRDRequirement, DesignDoc/RFC) added alongside the existing decision/capability nodes, (b) new typed edges (realized_by/ratified_by/implemented_by/conflicts_with), (c) content-hash drift anchors reusing the accounting-registry hashes the generated_face_drift check already hash-compares, and (d) a new rulepack loaded as DATA into the SAME evaluator — extending the guarantee from ADR-spec-masterplan-roadmap agreement to PRD-RFC-ADR-capability agreement. Reimplement nothing that exists; add node/edge kinds + rulepack + one anchor-fingerprint check.

category_comparison.category: Relational Wiki Solutions (graph/linked-doc wikis, ontology platforms, AST-fingerprint doc-binding)
category_comparison.verdict: ADOPT as the SUBSTRATE layer. Steal three deterministic primitives, reject every SaaS as substrate. From Backstage: derive reverse edges from a single declared field + continuous reconcile-and-stitch + orphan/reachability detection (already mirrored by staleness-reaper reachability). From Foundry: the graph is a PROJECTION of a source-of-truth, not a hand-maintained copy — bind the graph to reality (the code AST) so freshness is automatic, and rendered docs are build artifacts. From drift/fiberplane: content-addressed normalized-AST fingerprints on the edge that targets code, so a semantic change flags the doc stale but reformatting does not. Notion/Coda/Rovo/Foundry are references behind an owned port, never adopted.
category_comparison.best_for: The live typed node/edge store on governance/corpus/, reverse-edge derivation, orphan/reachability staleness, and the AST-fingerprint code-reality anchor that closes the doc-vs-code loop.

category_comparison.verdict: ADOPT as the SPINE and enforcement doctrine — highest-weight category. MIF/Structured-MADR = the schema-validated decision-NODE contract (status lifecycle, reciprocal-link referential integrity, immutability) that oyatie's ADR frontmatter already approximates. Spec-Kit SDD = the PRD→RFC→ADR→code forced-traceability chain + the NEEDS_CLARIFICATION ambiguity gate (structurally identical to the ambiguity≤0.2 doctrine) + cross-level 'spec requires X but plan assumes Y' contradiction flags — but reimplement those flags as DETERMINISTIC graph invariants, not Spec-Kit's LLM checks. Structurizr/ArchUnit = architecture-as-a-queryable-node + the net-new-only fitness-function ratchet (matches the merge-base ratchet doctrine exactly). Spectral/Vale = the neutral-engine + policy-as-data factoring the product MUST copy.
category_comparison.best_for: The node contract, the traceability edges, the promotion/ambiguity gate, the net-new ratchet, and the engine+ruleset-as-data portability shape.

category_comparison.category: AI-Driven Context Engines (LLM knowledge graphs + NLI contradiction + hybrid retrieval)
category_comparison.verdict: ADOPT ADVISORY-ONLY — never an enforcing gate. GraphRAG's typed-claim-with-status is a useful MODELING lens for the node schema (subject + status + provenance = content-hash of the source span), and the retrieve→NLI→judge pipeline is the right shape for SEMANTIC contradiction that deterministic invariants can't see (an ADR ruling that logically negates a PRD requirement in prose). But it runs as a non-blocking second opinion that files an issue for human triage — its verdicts are inadmissible as merge authority per the LLM-benchmark-evidence lesson. Cursor/Augment's Merkle content-hash freshness is real and already present in oyatie's scm-facts/accounting-registry — reuse it for the deterministic drift anchor. SHACL closed-world shapes are the right mental model for the fail-closed invariant evaluator, reimplemented as the owned Policy IR (do not pull an RDF/OWL toolchain).
category_comparison.best_for: Advisory semantic-contradiction triage (issue-filing, not gating), the typed-claim node schema lens, Merkle freshness reuse, and SHACL-shape thinking for the invariant evaluator.

synthesis.prd_rfc_adr_graph_model:
NODE KINDS (typed corpus nodes; extend the existing decision + capability nodes, do not replace them). Each node = {id, kind, subject_entity, status, provenance:{source_content_hash, span}}:
- PRDRequirement — id REQ-<svc>-NNN, harvested from the 1426 existing PRD.md files; status proposed|accepted|superseded; subject_entity is the capability/behavior it constrains.
- DesignDoc (oyatie's RFC tier — the DD-NNNN template already exists) — status draft|in-review|accepted|implemented|superseded.
- ADR — id ADR-NNNN, status proposed|accepted|deprecated|superseded (already a node in the current gate).
- Capability / CodeSymbol — already live + content-addressed in the corpus AST; this is the reality anchor, no new work.
- NEEDS_CLARIFICATION — an ambiguity node attached to any of the above; its unresolved existence BLOCKS the target's promotion past `accepted` (the ambiguity≤0.2 doctrine made structural).

EDGE KINDS (typed, directional, stored bidirectionally but AUTHORED FROM ONE END — Backstage's trick, so the two ends physically cannot disagree; each cross-tier edge carries an anchor {target_content_hash, stamped_at}):
- realized_by: PRDRequirement --realized_by--> DesignDoc (auto reverse: satisfies).
- ratified_by: DesignDoc --ratified_by--> ADR (auto reverse: realizes).
- implemented_by: ADR --implemented_by--> Capability/CodeSymbol (SOURCED from the existing ADR frontmatter affected_surfaces.crates — the edge already exists as data; auto reverse: implements). This edge carries the AST-fingerprint anchor.
- supersedes / superseded_by: within a kind, reciprocal — ALREADY enforced by the existing supersession_half_edge check; extend it to DesignDoc supersession.
- refines / derived_from: PRD→PRD or DD→DD lineage.
- depends_on: already on ADR frontmatter; promote to a first-class edge.
- conflicts_with: between any two same-subject nodes — the explicit contradiction edge; two nodes both `accepted` joined by conflicts_with is a fail-closed violation.
- clarifies: NEEDS_CLARIFICATION --clarifies--> {node} — promotion-blocking until resolved.

CARDINALITY / AGREEMENT SHAPES (SHACL-style, loaded as DATA into the evaluator; these ARE the invariants the gates below check):
- every `accepted` PRDRequirement MUST have ≥1 realized_by edge to an `accepted` DesignDoc.
- every `accepted` DesignDoc MUST have exactly 1 ratified_by edge to an `accepted` ADR OR carry an explicit trivial-exemption datum.
- every `accepted` ADR MUST have ≥1 implemented_by edge to a live Capability.
- status must agree along the chain: a requirement cannot be `accepted` while its ratifying ADR is `superseded` without a supersession edge to a live successor.
- no `conflicts_with` edge may join two `accepted` nodes; no two `accepted` ADRs may set the same capability property to different values.
- an `accepted` ADR must propagate to masterplan∧roadmap∧spec (already shipped) AND now also to its parent PRDRequirement + child DesignDoc.

The four disconnected markdown/JSON authorities (PRD.md, DD-NNNN, ADR-NNNN, JSON SSOT) collapse into ONE graph; their rendered markdown becomes a projection/build artifact compiled out of the graph — directly advancing the masterplan-v2 goal of reducing live md/json count.
enforcing_gates: unrealized_requirement (CONTRADICTION/traceability, BLOCKING, net-new ratchet): an `accepted` PRDRequirement with no realized_by edge to an `accepted` DesignDoc → RED. Pure structural graph query; new code in the existing evaluator.
unratified_design (CONTRADICTION/traceability, BLOCKING): an `accepted` DesignDoc with no ratified_by edge to an `accepted` ADR and no explicit trivial-exemption datum → RED.

unimplemented_decision (CONTRADICTION/traceability, BLOCKING): an `accepted` ADR with no implemented_by edge to a live Capability/CodeSymbol → RED. Reuses the existing affected_surfaces.crates data as the edge source.

conflicting_accepted_pair (CONTRADICTION, BLOCKING): two `accepted` nodes joined by a `conflicts_with` edge, OR two `accepted` ADRs setting the same capability property to different values → RED. This is the deterministic PRD-RFC-ADR contradiction detector.

status_disagreement (CONTRADICTION, BLOCKING — EXTEND the existing code): the chain PRD→RFC→ADR disagrees on status (e.g. requirement `accepted` while its ratifying ADR `superseded` with no live-successor supersession edge). Extends the current face set from ADR/spec/masterplan/roadmap to include PRD + DesignDoc.

unpropagated_decision (CONTRADICTION, BLOCKING — EXTEND the existing code): an `accepted` ADR that reaches SOME but not ALL required faces — now including its parent PRDRequirement + child DesignDoc, not only spec/masterplan/roadmap.

supersession_half_edge + dual_node_collision (CONTRADICTION, BLOCKING — REUSE existing codes): non-reciprocal supersession and one id shared by two files, extended to cover DesignDoc and PRDRequirement kinds, not just ADRs.

unresolved_clarification (CONTRADICTION/ambiguity gate, BLOCKING): a NEEDS_CLARIFICATION node blocking promotion of its target past `accepted` → RED. The ambiguity≤0.2 doctrine made a hard structural gate.

anchor_fingerprint_drift (STALENESS, BLOCKING on NET-NEW only): a cross-tier edge whose stamped target_content_hash ≠ the live corpus AST/capability node hash → the doc claim is stale → RED. Reuses the accounting-registry content hashes and the exact hash-compare mechanism the existing generated_face_drift check already runs; the predicate MUST evaluate the CANDIDATE tree (not the frozen merge-base) or it false-greens at PR tier — only the RATCHET baseline is merge-base-anchored.

untyped_anchor (STALENESS, BLOCKING — mirror untyped_staleness): a cross-tier edge carrying no anchor at all → RED, because an unanchorable claim can never be aged or verified; every claim MUST be bindable to reality.

orphan_node (STALENESS/archive-candidate, REPORT-NOT-REAP — REUSE orphan_decision + staleness-reaper reachability): a PRD/RFC/ADR node no longer reachable from any live root → flagged stale + archive-candidate via report → git mv → _archive, second-verifier-gated, never rm.

ADVISORY (NON-BLOCKING, files an issue, NEVER merge authority): semantic_contradiction_suspected — the retrieve→NLI→judge pass over sibling claims sharing a subject entity raises a suspected-contradiction issue for human/reviewer triage. Explicitly excluded from RED verdicts per the evidence-admissibility bar; it is a second opinion, not a gate.
synthesis.owned_substrate_design_notes:
SHIP SHAPE = neutral engine + policy-as-data, factored exactly like Spectral (linter core + ruleset-as-data), Vale (engine + style packs), and MIF (validator + conformance levels). Three neutral engine primitives ship once and know nothing about PRDs/ADRs/oyatie: (1) a typed content-addressed node/edge store (governance/corpus/); (2) a reconciler that recomputes anchor fingerprints + orphan reachability on every commit (the Backstage stitching loop / Foundry OMS cadence — event-driven, never periodic batch export); (3) a deterministic invariant evaluator that runs declarative graph-query shapes closed-world and emits keyed {code,key} findings. All domain nuance is data loaded per repo: the ONTOLOGY PACK (node kinds, edge kinds, cardinalities), the ANCHOR EXTRACTORS (per-language AST-fingerprint plugins behind a trait — Rust corpus AST first, others as adapters), the RULEPACK (which codes fire), and MIF-style conformance LEVELS 1/2/3 so any repo adopts incrementally and ratchets up.

DO NOT build a second gate — this is the single most important design constraint and the ponytail-correct move. The cross-artifact-agreement evaluator IS the invariant runtime; add node/edge kinds + a rulepack + one anchor-fingerprint check to it. The staleness-reaper already owns TTL + reachability + report-not-reap; the accounting-registry already owns content hashes; generated_face_drift already hash-compares faces. Reuse all three; write only the new node kinds, the new edges, and the drift anchor.

DOCS ARE BUILD ARTIFACTS: the graph is the single source; rendered ADR/PRD/RFC markdown + the ADR index + the JSON SSOT are PROJECTIONS compiled OUT of the graph (Foundry's 'projection, not a maintained copy'). This is what makes contradiction structurally impossible rather than merely detectable, and directly serves the masterplan-v2 md/json-reduction goal (countable live-authority reduction before/after).

DETERMINISTIC IS THE ONLY BLOCKING LAYER; LLM/NLI is advisory-only (evidence-admissibility). PORTS absorb transient infra (any embedding model, any NLI encoder, any vector index) behind owned traits whose shapes model the W5 destination, so a cutover to owned inference changes an adapter, not the engine. PORTABILITY / STRANGER'S-REPO TEST (the acceptance question): a Python or Go monorepo with zero ADRs loads a different ontology pack (REQUIREMENT→TEST→MODULE), a different anchor extractor, and a different rulepack, and gets identical contradiction+staleness gating with ZERO engine changes. If it can't, oyatie-specific nuance (ADR-0xxx numbering, baked capability names, oya tier names) has leaked into the engine and must be pushed back out into the pack. Author the whole thing as an IMPLEMENTATION of the existing corpus-pivot + cross-artifact-agreement ADR cluster, not a fresh design.
risks: Anchors are hand-declared, so drift coverage depends on discipline — a PRD/RFC/ADR with no implemented_by anchor silently escapes the staleness gate. Mitigation: the untyped_anchor gate makes an unanchorable accepted node itself a RED, forcing anchor declaration at promotion.

PR/push baseline asymmetry false-green: if the anchor_fingerprint_drift or traceability predicate is evaluated against the frozen merge-base instead of the candidate tree, it passes green while the candidate is actually stale (the documented gate-baseline asymmetry defect). Only the net-new RATCHET may be merge-base-anchored; every predicate must read the candidate tree.

Semantic contradiction that no deterministic invariant can see (an ADR whose prose logically negates a PRD requirement without any conflicts_with edge) will slip past the blocking layer. Accepted residual risk: the advisory NLI lane catches these but only files issues; closing it fully would require admitting LLM verdicts as merge authority, which the evidence-admissibility bar forbids.

The reconciler is the load-bearing AND genuinely hard part (Backstage issue #20030 — stale relations lingering after unregister is real, paged operational burden). Orphan/reachability cascade correctness must be tested with RED/GREEN fixtures, not assumed.

Migrating 1426 PRD.md + the DD/ADR corpus into typed nodes is a large one-time extraction with contradiction-surfacing risk (the migration will EXPOSE existing latent contradictions as new REDs). Adopt via MIF conformance levels — land at level 1 with the ratchet allowing existing debt, block only net-new, and ratchet up.

Rendering docs as build artifacts is a one-way door on the authoring workflow: authors stop editing markdown and edit the graph. If the projection/editor UX lags, it becomes friction that pushes authors back to side-docs — reintroducing the divergence the substrate exists to kill. The projection editor is on the critical path, not a follow-on.

Portability can silently rot: it is easy to hardcode an ADR-0xxx regex or an oya capability name into the evaluator 'just this once'. Ship the stranger's-repo test (a REQUIREMENT→TEST→MODULE fixture pack for a non-ADR repo) as a REQUIRED gate fixture so leakage of oyatie nuance into the engine fails CI.
